sentences: This is The Ten Largest, No.
7, Adulthood, by Hilma af Klint.
The sheet is more than three metres tall, nearly twice a person's height, and great yellow forms bloom across it like enormous flowers.
Few people had any idea it existed for most of the twentieth century.
The Swedish painter trained at the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Stockholm.
Through a spiritual circle with fellow women artists, she recorded in 1907 a call to make ten paradisaically beautiful paintings.
The series moves through four stages of life: childhood, youth, adulthood and old age.
She completed all ten in about forty days that autumn.
The adulthood sheets are painted on a soft lilac ground.
The large yellow form in the middle is marked with Roman numerals one and two.
Two rounded shapes overlap and merge into one, suggesting union and the balance of masculine and feminine that runs through the series.
From the single point where they meet, a third form opens downward like a bud.
Black curves gather together and spread out again, turning the rhythm of growth into something you can actually see.
It is a picture of becoming, not of being.
On the left, red petals and long tendrils stretch out, and spirals coil around the edges of the sheet.
These plant-like shapes speak of the deep connection between human life and the natural world.
The white loops on the right look like letters, yet they spell nothing you can read.
Invented words, or words she believed came from the spirit world, flow through her paintings in this looping script.
Painted in tempera on paper, the sheets were probably laid out on the studio floor because of their size.
Her fellow artist Cornelia Cederberg, a member of the same spiritual circle, helped with the work, following her direction.
It came years before Kandinsky's first abstractions.
But in 1932 af Klint asked that her work be kept from the public for a long time.
She marked her notebooks not to be opened until twenty years after her death.
So for decades these paintings were almost unknown.
When the Guggenheim in New York gave her a retrospective in 2018, more than 600,000 people came.
It became the most visited exhibition in the museum's history.
Step back and look up at the whole sheet.
Can you feel the yellow forms swelling and gathering, almost like breathing?
If your own adulthood had a shape and a colour, what would it be?
